artifacts.summary: Re-measured --compare threading surface, the measured layer-lint.sh/Books.Meta gate contracts, the books-extension binding site, and a six-phase implementation decomposition for the advisory --gate flag.

memory_candidates.content: check-extension-docs.sh Rule E (check_referenced_scripts_declared) extracts every `<name>.sh`/`.sql` token from an extension's commands/*.md, skills/*/SKILL.md, agents/*.md, README.md and EXTENSION.md and hard-fails unless that name is declared in core's provides.scripts/provides.hooks, ANY extension's provides.scripts, or the extension's own provides.hooks (exact OR basename match). scripts/** and context/** are NOT scanned. Consequence: an extension that wants to invoke a script owned by the CONSUMING repository (e.g. interface/scripts/layer-lint.sh) can never satisfy Rule E by naming it in a doc location. The sanctioned answer is a resolve-and-passthrough wrapper script declared in provides.scripts; books-certify.sh is the shipped reference implementation and says so in its own header (resolve git rev-parse --show-toplevel with a pwd fallback, locate the real driver, exit 3 with an actionable message when absent, exec with verbatim argument forwarding). Rule Q separately fails on any file under scripts/ not named in provides.scripts, matched by FULL RELATIVE PATH (so tests/test-foo.sh, not a basename).

The advisory-only /orchestrate flag pattern (--compare, and now --gate) has a fixed seven-file threading surface that must be re-measured each time because line numbers drift: parse-command-args.sh needs FIVE edits (header doc comment, initializer, the =~ detector, the FOCUS_PROMPT sed strip chain, and the export list -- the strip chain is the one most often forgotten, and omitting it leaks the flag into focus text); orchestrate-cycle-plan.sh needs declaration + parse arm + ONE forwarding line whose `[ "$g" = "implement" ]` conjunct is the entire mechanism scoping the flag away from research/plan dispatches; orchestrate-build-dispatch.sh needs declaration + parse arm + a CONDITIONAL emission so a no-flag dispatch file stays byte-identical to one built before the flag existed (its test suite asserts "differs by exactly one added line"); plus commands/orchestrate.md's Options table, skill-orchestrate/SKILL.md's Move 1, and return-metadata-file.md's optional block. build_args is composed at exactly one site, so there is no second forwarding path. The advisory MUST-NOTs belong INSIDE the agent step's own text, not in a separate section, specifically so a later editor cannot fold the advisory branch into the status-downgrading failure enumeration.

A lint whose rules are regexes over file paths can PASS VACUOUSLY -- scanning many files while no rule's file-half matches any of them -- and neither its exit code nor its summary line distinguishes that from a real pass. Measured in Logos/Verification: `bash interface/scripts/layer-lint.sh books` prints `[ok] layer import rule (62 modules, 119 imports, ...)` and exits 0 while 0 of 9 rules apply to anything under books/. Detect vacuity WITHOUT copying the rule set: source the rules file in a SUBSHELL (it may `exit 1` during sourcing -- layer-rules.sh does, when its queue-model derivation yields nothing, which also means an exit 1 is not necessarily a violation), then for each rule take field 1 of the ';'-delimited entry as the file-half regex and grep the scanned path list against it; rules_matched == 0 means vacuous. Report pass_vacuous as a first-class status, never collapsed into pass.
